evidenceMethod: repository inspection of CAPITAL-AI Stripe server integration
production Supabase Edge Function read-only inspection
existing Stripe DPA and Data Transfers Addendum contract evidence

observedProductFlows.notes: Current repository code creates server-side subscription Checkout Sessions and Stripe Customers. Completed livemode Checkout Sessions were observed in the connected production account.
At least one succeeded livemode charge in the connected account reports payment_method_details.type=link. This does not establish that the current repository checkout configuration still offers Link.

webhookDestinations.receiverAuthentication: Stripe webhook signature verified with constructEventAsync before event handling
webhookDestinations.unhandledEventBehavior: Other valid Stripe events are parsed, their event type is logged, and the function returns success without generic event persistence.
webhookDestinations.finding: The Stripe endpoint currently subscribes to all events although the production function intentionally handles only three event types. Transport exposure is therefore broader than the receiver's functional processing need.

webhookDestinations.receiverEvidence: Repository server/stripe.ts implements subscription/invoice webhook processing and persists subscription/profile state through Supabase admin access.
webhookDestinations.finding: Stripe event data is also delivered to the Render application path, creating a second production webhook destination that must be considered in the data-flow inventory.

currentOfficialSource.changeFinding: The current official list differs from the 2025-12-20 snapshot and includes additional general cloud subprocessors including Microsoft Corporation (Microsoft Azure) and Snowflake, Inc.

subprocessorMapping.reason: Stripe lists AWS as a general cloud subprocessor for Business User, Representative and End Customer data; available evidence does not identify which CAPITAL-AI records are hosted by this specific provider.
Current Stripe source lists Azure as a general cloud subprocessor; no CAPITAL-AI-specific provider routing evidence was available.
Current Stripe source lists Snowflake as a cloud subprocessor; no CAPITAL-AI-specific provider routing evidence was available.
The DE production account enters the DPA with SPEL under the Stripe DPA structure.
The DPA expressly states that, to provide the Services, User transfers Personal Data to Stripe, LLC in the United States.

nonObservedScopeRule: Service-specific subprocessors for these products are not classified as actual CAPITAL-AI data recipients merely because they appear on Stripe's global provider list.

mechanismEvidence: EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework where applicable
EEA SCCs according to the Data Transfers Addendum when applicable/fallback

onwardSubprocessorTransfers.reason: The global Stripe list identifies potential third-country subprocessors, but current evidence does not prove the exact infrastructure/support route for each CAPITAL-AI record or service invocation.

openFindings.finding: The Supabase Stripe webhook endpoint is subscribed to all Stripe events while its function handles only checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.updated and customer.subscription.deleted.
openFindings.recommendedAction: Narrow the Stripe webhook endpoint's enabled event set to the receiver's required events after confirming no external consumer depends on the wildcard subscription.

openFindings.finding: Stripe currently delivers production webhook data to both Supabase Edge Functions and the Render Finance service. Validate whether both paths remain intentionally required and define one canonical ownership model to avoid duplicated processing/drift.

DPA/DTA and current provider-list evidence establish contractual mechanisms and potential onward recipients, but a CAPITAL-AI-specific assessment of actual onward transfers and supplementary-measure/TIA necessity remains incomplete.

limitations: No production Stripe configuration was changed during this evidence review.
The global Stripe subprocessor list identifies potential recipients but does not expose per-customer infrastructure routing.
A successful Stripe Link transaction proves use of that payment method for at least one observed transaction, not its continued availability in the current checkout configuration.
This flow mapping does not claim GDPR compliance or a completed TIA.
